fields.default: At least, that is what they said. In August 2024, I left the Netherlands for my first big journey into Asia. I was excited, of course, but a little nervous too. It would be my first time away from home for more than five months, with three of them spent discovering Thailand as part of my International Business degree.

fields.label: One fun link between campus and everyday life: PIM was founded under CP ALL, the company that operat

fields.default: In my first Polarsteps entry from Pak Kret, I was still adjusting to the heat. Our first Monday brought an introduction and a tour of campus. Outside class, the street-food stalls and familiar 7-Eleven signs were quickly becoming part of everyday life.

fields.label: In my last week in Thailand, my parents came to visit me and see the country. By then, I was sad to
fields.default: In my last week in Thailand, my parents came to visit me and see the country. By then, I was sad to be leaving. I ended my Polarsteps notes certain of one thing: this would not be my last time in Thailand.

fields.label: So, is Thailand the land of smiles? For me, it was also a place of contrasts: busy streets and quiet
fields.default: So, is Thailand the land of smiles? For me, it was also a place of contrasts: busy streets and quiet water, late nights and early adventures, new flavours and familiar routines seen in a new light. I arrived for an exchange and left with a wider view of the world—and a reminder that travel is less about ticking places off a map than learning to see through someone else’s perspective.

fields.label: Bangkok made a big first impression. In Chinatown, the colour and energy of the streets pulled me to
fields.default: Bangkok made a big first impression. In Chinatown, the colour and energy of the streets pulled me towards the food stalls. I tried fresh local dishes, along with some more unusual bites—including insects. There was always something new to look at, smell or taste.

fields.label: I remember some meals costing around 37 to 80 baht—roughly one or two euros at the time. That felt i
fields.default: I remember some meals costing around 37 to 80 baht—roughly one or two euros at the time. That felt incredibly affordable from my European point of view. But a low price for a visitor can still be a meaningful amount for someone who lives and works locally. It made me think twice about calling a place “cheap” as if everyone experiences its prices in the same way.

fields.label: One September entry took me from temple visits to the view from MahaNakhon. Another brought Ancient
fields.default: One September entry took me from temple visits to the view from MahaNakhon. Another brought Ancient City: a huge park to explore, and I happily chose a golf cart. Bangkok kept giving me a different way to spend a day.

fields.label: I got to know Bangkok’s nightlife, and weekend trips to Pattaya brought a different change of pace:
fields.default: I got to know Bangkok’s nightlife, and weekend trips to Pattaya brought a different change of pace: evenings out, visits to animal parks and time to explore the city’s landmarks. The intricately carved [Sanctuary of Truth](https://thailand.go.th/public/issue-focus-detail/sanctuary-of-truth-pattaya) stood out for its scale and detailed wooden architecture. Back in Bangkok, seeing Wat Arun glowing beside the river after dark gave the city another mood altogether.

fields.label: If Bangkok was constant motion, Khao Sok was the reset. My Polarsteps notes bring those four days ba
fields.default: If Bangkok was constant motion, Khao Sok was the reset. My Polarsteps notes bring those four days back clearly: river tubing and a jungle walk on our first evening, then a boat out to the lake for an overnight stay. We went kayaking, walked to waterfalls and got up early for sunrise on the water. After the lake, we returned to the jungle for one more night and a long morning hike. The landscape alone was enough to slow me down.

fields.label: For roughly half our stay, there was no internet. I expected that to be inconvenient; instead, it fe
fields.default: For roughly half our stay, there was no internet. I expected that to be inconvenient; instead, it felt like a gift. No steady stream of notifications, no doom-scrolling—just the people around me and the place we had come to experience. I remember how good it felt to be properly present.

fields.label: Phuket was the starting point for this trip south. After four days in Khao Sok, we returned there fo
fields.default: Phuket was the starting point for this trip south. After four days in Khao Sok, we returned there for a night in a cabin hostel before taking the boat to Phi Phi. We met new people, spent time on the water and walked up to the lookout point. The sea and steep green islands gave us a completely different view. My phone even ended up in the water on a boat trip—a less welcome memory, but thankfully I still had everything. Inland, Ayutthaya offered another kind of perspective. It was once the capital of Siam and became a major centre of trade and diplomacy; today, its temple ruins make that history feel close enough to walk through. The city is recognised as a [UNESCO World Heritage site](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/576).

fields.label: I’m a big animal lover, so visiting a wildlife park or zoo is something I often try to make room for
fields.default: I’m a big animal lover, so visiting a wildlife park or zoo is something I often try to make room for when I travel. Thailand gave me plenty of animal encounters to remember—from an elephant up close to a capybara visit and seeing the hippos that included Moo Deng. They added a playful, personal thread to a journey full of cities, landscapes and culture.
